text: Check Used by What can still go wrong Proof checker (Lean 4, Isabelle, Rocq) miniF2F, PutnamBench, ArXivLean, AlphaProof The formal statement can misstate the problem; a "with answer" track hands the prover the answer Answer computed by code FrontierMath (the model submits a Python function answer() that returns, for example, an integer or a sympy object) The reference answer itself: Epoch's v2 fixed 135 of 350 problems and removed 12 more Exact integer AIME (0 to 999), GSM8K Guessing (1 in 1,000 on AIME), answer-key errors (GSM8K-Platinum removed 110 test items), a parser that misses the final answer Normalised expression MATH (boxed LaTeX), HMMT under MathArena Equivalent forms judged different, or different forms judged equal LLM judge Omni-MATH (GPT-4o), HLE The judge is part of the instrument: its errors become the score's errors Human graders IMO, USAMO, MathArena proof tracks Cost, small samples, and who graded: officially certified, the lab's own panel, or an AI grader FrontierMath adds a design rule worth stealing: a problem must not give more than a 1% chance of guessing the answer without doing most of the work ( Glazer et al., section 2 ), which is why its answers are large, unobvious objects rather than small integers.

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., OpenAI, 27 Oct 2021 ) is "8.5K high quality grade school math problems created by human problem writers", each needing 2 to 8 steps of basic arithmetic; "a bright middle school student should be able to solve every problem".
label: core
key: 8.5K high quality grade school math problems

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: The released split is 7,473 training and 1,319 test problems ( Hugging Face, MIT licence ); the paper rounds them to 7.5K and 1K.
label: core

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: Each solution ends in #### 14 , a single number, graded by exact match, and carries calculator annotations such as <<62-48=14>> .
label: core

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: The paper's own method was already a sampling protocol: generate 100 candidate solutions and let a trained verifier pick one.
label: depth

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: Its best, GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with a verifier, scored 55% (the figure PaLM later quoted as the prior best).

text: No 2026 frontier card reports GSM8K, so there is no current frontier figure; the last ones were mid-90s (GPT-4o 95.2% and o1-mini 95.1% on the full test set in GSM-Symbolic's Table 1 ).

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: And the contamination evidence is family by family, not frontier-wide: GSM1k, a fresh look-alike set of 1,205 human-written problems kept private (50 are printed in its appendix), found drops of up to 8% and systematic overfitting in several families, but "many models, especially those on the frontier, show minimal signs of overfitting" ( Zhang et al., v4 ).
label: core

text: Part of the ceiling is the key, not the models: GSM8K-Platinum re-checked 219 flagged test questions, removed 110 and relabelled 10, leaving 1,209 ( MadryLab, March 2025 ).
label: core

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: GSM-Symbolic: the same question, perturbed Apple's GSM-Symbolic ( Mirzadeh et al., 7 Oct 2024 ) turned 100 GSM8K test questions into templates: names, family members and numbers become variables with ranges and conditions (for instance, the answer must be a whole number).

label: core

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: The dramatic part holds up: P2 and NoOp cut every model, even strong ones (o1-preview from 94.9% on the full GSM8K test to 77.4% on NoOp), and models "blindly convert" a statement such as "five of them were a bit smaller" into a subtraction.

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: The paper's other headline, that accuracy "varies" across the 50 sets of renamed and renumbered questions, is weaker than it sounds: the reported spreads (about 2 to 3.5 points) are smaller than the roughly 4 points binomial chance alone gives at 100 items derived .
label: core

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: Ivanova et al. re-tested the paper's numbers and found only 3 of 25 models with a statistically significant GSM8K to GSM-Symbolic drop (Fisher exact test), and the growing spread on harder variants "a trivial consequence of the decrease in probabilities"; but NoOp was significant for all 25 ( ICLR 2025 blog post ).
label: core

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: The authors answered in their v2 appendix that a model that truly understood a question should not flip when only a name changes, so variance itself is the finding.
label: depth

section: grade school: gsm8k and what broke it
text: Both readings agree on the practical lesson: a single GSM8K accuracy cannot tell understanding from pattern matching, and irrelevant information is where pattern matching shows.

text: Competition math: MATH, MATH-500, Omni-MATH MATH ( Hendrycks et al., 5 Mar 2021 ) collects 12,500 problems from high-school competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME and similar), 7,500 for training and 5,000 for test, in seven subjects (prealgebra, algebra, number theory, counting and probability, geometry with diagrams written in the Asymptote language, intermediate algebra, precalculus) and five difficulty levels.
label: core

text: Every problem has a full LaTeX solution ending in a \boxed{} answer, "unique after normalization", so it is graded by exact match after normalising the expression rather than by text overlap.
label: core

text: At launch, models scored 3.0% to 6.9%; the paper's human check was small: on 20 problems a computer-science PhD student who "does not especially like mathematics" got 8 (40%) and a three-time IMO gold medallist 18 (90%), missing two "exclusively due to small errors of arithmetic".
label: depth

text: The climb: Minerva 540B 33.6% with one sample and 50.3% with a majority vote over samples, a different protocol on the same set ( Lewkowycz et al., June 2022, Table 3 ); GPT-4 42.5% four-shot (March 2023); o1 94.8% on MATH-500 (September 2024).
label: depth

text: Epoch AI's own runs on the hardest level (1,324 Level 5 test problems) go from 22.97% for GPT-4 (June 2023) to 98.13% for GPT-5 (high), run in October 2025 (the parent's Saturation timeline tab draws all three series).
label: depth

text: On MATH-500, o3 scores 99.2% and the top five sit between 98.2% and 99.2%; the same study flags MATH-500 as contaminated ( Akhtar et al., ICML 2026, Table 6 ).
label: core

text: Where MATH-500 comes from matters more than it looks.
label: core

text: OpenAI's process-reward work needed more training problems, so it moved 4,500 of the 5,000 MATH test problems into the PRM800K training set and evaluated only on the remaining 500, "selected uniformly at random" ( Lightman et al., Let's Verify Step by Step ).
label: core

text: Those 500 became the standard subset, and the other 4,500 test problems have sat in a public training set with step-level labels since May 2023: a full-MATH-test score after that date is not clean.
label: core
key: A full-MATH-test score after May 2023 is not clean

text: Omni-MATH ( Gao et al., 10 Oct 2024 ) answered MATH's saturation with 4,428 olympiad-level problems in over 33 sub-domains and more than 10 difficulty levels.
label: core

text: Its answers are too varied for string matching, so the main leaderboard is graded by GPT-4o, with an open judge model (Omni-Judge) and a rule-gradable subset beside it.
label: core

text: At launch o1-mini led with 60.54% and o1-preview 52.55%; the official board still shows those September 2024 rows ( omni-math.github.io , read 4 Oct 2026), so it is a dormant board, and any newer figure is someone's own run with someone's own judge.
label: core

section: contests as benchmarks: aime, hmmt and matharena
text: MathArena ( Balunović, Dekoninck et al., ETH Zurich and INSAIT ) made this a protocol: extract the problems and answers as soon as a contest ends; run every selected model four times per problem with one fixed prompt ("Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.

text: The answer is an integer between 0 and 999 inclusive."); parse the boxed answer with a rule-based parser, with flagged parses reviewed by hand; report accuracy as the mean over all answers (pass@1) with no majority voting; publish cost and tokens; and mark every model released after the contest date as possibly contaminated.

text: Here is the hardest AIME 2025 problem with the four real answers of nine models, graded three ways: One sample (pass@1) Vote of 4 (maj@4) Any of 4 (pass@4) Real answers from MathArena/aime_2025_outputs , runs 1 to 4 in order; "none" means the parser found no final answer (counted wrong). maj@4 is computed exactly: the most common answer among the four wins, and a tie is split evenly between the tied answers (so a 2 to 2 tie with the right answer counts one half). pass@4 asks whether any of the four is right, which needs an oracle that knows the answer.

text: Research math: FrontierMath Construction.
label: fat

text: FrontierMath ( Glazer et al., Epoch AI, 7 Nov 2024 ) is a set of new, unpublished problems written and vetted by more than 60 mathematicians (collectively 14 IMO gold medals and one Fields Medal; Terence Tao contributed several). "Solving a typical problem requires multiple hours of effort from a researcher in the relevant branch of mathematics, and for the upper end questions, multiple days." Each answer is a definite object checked by code, built to be guessproof.
label: core

text: In Epoch's harness the model can run Python (sympy, numpy, mpmath and a few other libraries), must submit a Python function answer() that returns its answer within 30 seconds, and has a hard limit of 1,000,000 tokens, with forced submission from 660,000 ( Epoch AI, methodology ).
label: core

text: At launch "current state-of-the-art AI models solve under 2% of problems" (about 6% for the best model when any of eight runs counts, in the paper's appendix), and Tao, interviewed for the paper, expected the problems to "resist AIs for several years at least".
label: core

text: The core set is graded into three tiers by difficulty, and Tier 4 was added in 2025 as "an expansion set of 50 problems designed to vastly exceed the difficulty of even the Tier 3 problems", written by professors and postdocs ( Epoch AI, Tiers 1-4 about ).
label: core
key: vastly exceed the difficulty of even the Tier 3 problems

text: Formal proofs: miniF2F and PutnamBench A formal benchmark asks for a proof that a proof assistant accepts, so grading is mechanical and a wrong proof cannot pass. miniF2F ( Zheng, Han and Polu, OpenAI, 31 Aug 2021 ) has 488 problem statements from the AIME, AMC and IMO and from school and undergraduate courses, split 244 validation and 244 test, formalised in Metamath and Lean, partly in Isabelle and HOL Light; its baseline was GPT-f.
